source: CK-12 Physical Science Concepts for Middle School, Section 15.1, CC-BY-NC
notes: Class B document (13 units). Covers wave properties (amplitude, wavelength, frequency) and transverse/longitudinal distinction. One ECU for the worked example.

units.label: Hook: slinky demonstration (video)
units.content_summary: Video of a slinky being shaken to produce visible transverse waves, then pushed/pulled to produce longitudinal (compression) waves side by side for comparison.

units.label: Learning Objectives (text)
units.content_summary: Objectives: define wave properties (amplitude, wavelength, frequency, period); distinguish transverse from longitudinal waves; calculate wave speed.

units.label: Wave properties definitions (text)
units.content_summary: Amplitude: maximum displacement from rest. Wavelength (λ): distance between two successive crests. Frequency (f): number of waves per second, in Hertz. Period (T): time for one full wave cycle, T=1/f.

units.label: Labeled wave diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Sine wave diagram with amplitude, wavelength, crest, and trough all labeled with arrows.

units.label: Transverse vs longitudinal (text)
units.content_summary: Transverse wave: particles move perpendicular to wave direction (e.g. light, slinky shake). Longitudinal wave: particles move parallel to wave direction (e.g. sound, slinky push-pull).

units.label: Transverse/longitudinal diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Side-by-side diagrams: transverse wave showing perpendicular particle motion; longitudinal wave showing compressions and rarefactions.

units.label: Wave speed formula (text)
units.content_summary: Wave speed equation: v = f × λ (speed = frequency × wavelength). Units: m/s = Hz × m.

units.label: Worked example: calculate wave speed (text)
units.content_summary: Problem: a wave has frequency 5 Hz and wavelength 2m. Find speed. Solution: v = 5 × 2 = 10 m/s.

units.label: Worked example diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Wave diagram with wavelength marked as 2m and frequency label, showing calculation result v=10m/s annotated.

units.label: Real-world application: sound and light (text)
units.content_summary: Sound waves are longitudinal, travel ~343 m/s in air. Light waves are transverse, travel at 3×10^8 m/s in vacuum. Both obey v=fλ, explaining why thunder is heard after lightning is seen.

units.label: Practice problems (text)
units.content_summary: Three problems: calculate speed given f and λ; calculate wavelength given v and f; classify a described wave as transverse or longitudinal.
